title: Chewy Ginger Molasses Cookies
description: Soft, thick, chewy molasses cookies warmed with ginger, cinnamon and cloves, rolled in sugar so the tops crackle. A big batch that's made for holiday cookie trays.
equipment: parchment paper or silicone baking mats

items.note: the source weighs flour at 142 g per cup

step_groups.name: Make the dough
steps: Whisk the flour, baking soda, ginger, cinnamon, cloves and salt together in a medium bowl.
In a separate bowl, beat the butter with both sugars on medium-high speed until pale and fluffy, about 2 minutes, scraping down the bowl as needed.
Turn the mixer to medium-low and beat in the eggs one at a time, then the molasses, mixing until each is combined.
Add the dry mixture a little at a time and beat just until no dry flour remains.

step_groups.name: Chill
steps: Pack the dough into an airtight container and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, until fully cold and firm. Don't skip this: the butter and molasses make the dough spread badly if it's warm.

step_groups.name: Shape and bake
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and line a sheet pan with parchment or a silicone mat.
Roll the cold dough into balls about 1 inch (2.5 cm) across. Roll each ball in a small bowl of sugar until fully coated and set them on the pan with room to spread.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes, until the tops just start to crack. They'll crack more as they cool.
Let the cookies rest on the pan for 4 to 5 minutes, then move them to wire racks to cool completely.

notes: Yield is an estimate: the source calls this a very large batch but doesn't give a count. Halve the recipe (½× button) for a normal batch.
The baking soda amount is correct for this big batch, per the source.
Variations: fold in chopped crystallized ginger for extra bite, or finish with a thin glaze or cream cheese frosting.
White whole wheat flour can stand in for all-purpose.
storage: Keep in a sealed container at room temperature for up to 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months.
